overview: This single-page file consists of a list-of-papers sheet for the State Department subject “Beverages—Japan.” It records a despatch by Joseph C. Grew concerning the labeling of Japanese wines and the absence in Japan of certificates attesting their character, place of origin, and legality of manufacture, while directing readers to a related liquor file under decimal number 811.114 Liquor/901.

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan; author of the referenced despatch

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Grew despatch on wine labeling in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes a Grew despatch reporting that Japan did not issue certificates verifying the character, origin, and legality of manufacture of its wines.
subfiles.summary: This list-of-papers sheet contains one entry under the subject “Beverages—Japan.” It identifies despatch no. 1191 from Grew, dated February 21, 1935, concerning wine labeling and the lack of Japanese certificates attesting product character, place of origin, and lawful manufacture. The entry refers the reader to decimal file 811.114 Liquor/901 for the substantive documentation.

interest: The sheet is useful primarily as an archival finding aid: it preserves the subject, despatch number, author, date, and cross-reference for a substantive document filed elsewhere. It also points to an administrative obstacle in international wine trade—the absence of Japanese official certification for origin, character, and lawful manufacture—and illustrates how related commercial and regulatory material was dispersed across the State Department’s decimal filing system. The printed year appears to have been OCR-misread as 1925; 1935 is consistent with Grew’s service in Japan and the stated 1930–1949 record series.
